chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Faddal, from al-Ma'la ibn Khunais, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

The Nasib (hostile one) is not the one who is hostile to us, the Ahl al-Bayt, because you do not find anyone saying: 'I hate Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad,' but the Nasib is the one who is hostile to you, while he knows that you befriend us or dissociate yourselves from our enemies. And he (peace be upon him) said: The one who satisfies an enemy of ours has certainly killed an ally of ours.

key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: The Nasib, one who is hostile or envious, specifically towards the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.تَتَوَلَّوْنَا: You befriend us / show love to us

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Nasib in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to clarify that 'Nasib' (enemy of the Ahl al-Bayt) is defined by specific knowledge and intent rather than mere general dislike, emphasizing that true enmity involves actively satisfying the Imams' enemies. This distinction highlights the Shia concept of *Tawalla* (affinity) and *Tabarra* (disaffiliation), where spiritual allegiance is tied to the Imams' specific adversaries. The concluding statement underscores the gravity of political and social alignment, equating the satisfaction of an enemy with the death of a friend.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I was told by my paternal uncle, Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasem, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Faddal, from Mu’alla bin Khunais, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:

The nasib is not the one who is hostile to us, the Household, because you do not find anyone saying: «I hate Muhammed and the Family of Muhammed», however, the nasib is the one who is hostile to you, while he knows that you befriend us or dissociate yourselves from our enemies. He, peace be upon him, also said: The one who satisfies an enemy to us, has certainly killed an ally of us.
